claim: A GB300 NVL72 rack contains 72 B300 GPUs across 18 compute trays and can require up to 142 kW.
The article’s reference case treats 1 GW as total facility nameplate, not IT nameplate or an interconnection request.
notes: Boundary is explicit and alternatives are calculated separately.

claim: At PUE 1.145 and 10% external IT overhead, 1 GW facility nameplate converts to 873.36 MW of IT and 793.97 MW of GB300 rack nameplate.
The reference case supports about 5,591 GB300 racks and 402,574 installed B300 GPUs.
notes: Fractional racks are modeling output; deployment count should be read as approximately 5,591.

claim: The sensitivity band is about 355,819 to 434,856 GPUs across PUE 1.25/overhead 14% to PUE 1.10/overhead 6%.
notes: Assumption range is scenario design, not a measured industry interval.

claim: If 1 GW instead means IT nameplate, the same 10% external IT overhead supports about 460,948 B300 GPUs.
notes: PUE is not applied because the boundary is already IT.

claim: A 1 GW interconnection request at 50% average utilization corresponds to 500 MW average facility demand and 4.38 TWh/year, but does not determine installed GPU count.
notes: 50% is LBNL’s illustrative estimate and is not universal.

claim: The eight-SU reference BOM includes 55 compute/converged switches and 16 OOB switches for 576 GPUs.
Using SN5600 passive-cable power, those external switches total at least 53.27 kW, 4.69% of eight racks’ 1.136 MW nameplate.
notes: Lower bound excludes optics, storage, support servers, and larger-cluster tiers.

claim: Using the SN5610 fully optical typical figure as a comparator, switch power rises to 115.97 kW, 10.21% of rack nameplate.
notes: Comparator, not a claim that all ports are populated or that BOM naming is resolved.

claim: NVIDIA’s current documentation is internally inconsistent on SN5600 versus SN5610 naming.
At roughly 1,024 nodes and above, NVIDIA introduces a super-spine, so eight-SU network power cannot be linearly extrapolated to a gigawatt campus.
notes: Supports range rather than point estimate for external IT overhead.

claim: The reference fleet provides 3.53 billion powered-on GPU-hours per year before utilization.
At 80% training utilization, the reference fleet yields about 2.82 billion full-load-equivalent GPU-hours; at 20% inference utilization, about 0.705 billion.
notes: Computational utilization is not revenue utilization.

claim: Installed accelerators, average electrical draw, computational utilization, and paid utilization are separate quantities.
No exact installed-fleet estimate is defensible when a source says only “1 GW” without defining boundary, status, and time basis.
